get.description:
The thread. With `language`, template-based outgoing messages are re-rendered in that language (patient language switch).

The re-render uses the slots stored with each message, so its reading and dates are the ones from when it was created.
A message stored before slots were kept, or one that cannot render in the language, keeps its stored text.

ActionRequest.title: ActionRequest
ActionRequest.description: `payload` is validated against the model for `action` (see components.schemas *Payload) after role and state checks.

DiaryOut.title: DiaryOut
DiaryOut.description: Wearable data is a diary only. wearable_used_for_bp is always false.

I18nText.title: I18nText
I18nText.description: The same display text in every supported language. The front end picks the key for its current language.

PersonRef.title: PersonRef
PersonRef.description: A person shown to a reader. `name` has no role in brackets; `role` is the job title, for example `nurse coordinator`.

ReadingSource.title: ReadingSource
ReadingSource.description: Blood pressure values come only from a validated cuff or ambulatory monitor. There is no wearable source.

ReplyOption.title: ReplyOption
ReplyOption.description: One reply the patient can send now. `meaning_key` is for the front end's own label (reply.yes, reply.option_a, ...).

SendRequest.title: SendRequest
SendRequest.description: Send a stored draft. Free text is refused: the server re-renders the template and re-validates AI wording.

TeachBackOut.title: TeachBackOut
TeachBackOut.description: The teach-back question as structured fields in one language. The front end never parses message text.

ClosePayload.description: Fields are optional here so the closure gate, not the schema, explains what is missing.
